parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module does not use one consistent persistence boundary. SchedulingService reads and writes data only through the persistence layer's DAO abstractions, AppointmentDao and PatientDao, injected through its constructor. It turns each row into a domain entity (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment) before applying any rule. VisitNotesService does not do this. It injects PrismaService, which is the ORM client, and calls prisma.visitNote.create and prisma.visitNote.findMany directly. It builds plain VisitNote records from those rows inline and uses no DAO or entity at all. This goes around the DAO/repository style that the rest of the module uses, so the module mixes two different ways of reaching persistence. Both candidate flags (VisitNotesService.ts:13-15 and :20) match the source. The two services both deal with appointments, so splitting them into unrelated concerns is a weak argument. The failure rests on VisitNotesService going around the module's abstraction. A smaller point: in SchedulingService, the code that turns an appointment row into an Appointment is written out twice, once in book (the forPractitioner map) and once in cancel. This is a copied mapping, not a business rule, so it is noted as supporting evidence only. Confidence is moderate because the source shown contains no visit-note DAO.

violations.message: VisitNotesService goes around the module's DAO style of reaching persistence. It also skips domain entities and maps rows to VisitNote inline, so the module does not use its abstractions consistently.
